function.name: EventSettingsApi_create_website_alert_config
function.description: Creates a configuration for website alerting within the system, allowing users to define conditions under which alerts should be triggered for a website. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name for the website alert configuration.

description.description: A detailed description for the website alert configuration.

severity.description: The severity level of the alert when triggered.

triggering.description: Flag indicating whether the alert configuration should also trigger an incident.

websiteId.description: The unique identifier of the website for which the alert configuration is created.

tagFilterExpression.description: A boolean expression used to filter the scope of website beacons based on tags.

granularity.description: The evaluation granularity in seconds used for detection of threshold violations.

rule.description: The type of rule this alert configuration pertains to, such as 'traffic spike' or 'downtime'.

threshold.description: The threshold value that, when exceeded, will trigger the alert. This is a float type value.

timeThreshold.description: The time duration in seconds during which the threshold must be exceeded to trigger the alert.

alertChannelIds.description: A list of alert channel IDs defined in Instana to which the alert notifications will be sent.

message.content:
I’m afraid I don’t have direct visibility into your “delta” deployment’s current Instana Alert (formerly *Infrana* Alert) configuration – there isn’t a built‑in way for me to pull that out of thin air. If you can share a bit more detail, I’ll gladly walk you through exactly where to look: | What you might need | How to get it | |---------------------|---------------| | **Instana Agent & UI Version** | Log into the Instana web console → `Administration` > `System Information`. That page lists both the agent and core platform releases. | | **Installed Alert Rules** | Use the REST API:
`GET https:///api/v1/alerts/configs`
with proper auth (`X-Instana-License-Key`). You’ll see each rule’s `version`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, etc. | | **Specific Rule Versions** | If you’re interested in a particular rule ID, hit:
`GET .../api/v1/alerts/configs/` | ### Quick example (curl) ```bash export INSTA_HOST="https://your.instana.host" export LICENSE_KEY="YOUR_LICENSE_KEY" curl -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-instana-license-key:$LICENSE_KEY" \ "$INSTA_HOST/api/v1/alerts/configs" | jq . ``` This returns JSON objects similar to: ```json { "id": "12345", "name": "Traffic Spike", "ruleType": "TRAFFIC_SPIKE", "severity": 2, "lastUpdated": "2025-04-12T08:23:00Z", ... } ``` --- #### If you meant *which software package versions* are installed on the host machines running the Instana agents (“delta”), you’d typically check the OS package manager: - On Debian/Ubuntu: ```bash dpkg -l | grep instana-agent ``` - On RHEL/CentOS: ```bash rpm -qa | grep instana-agent ``` That will show entries like `instana-agent-7.8.3`. Let me know which angle you were after—agent binaries, UI/API release, or specific alert rule definitions—and I can tailor the instructions further!
